name: Improve MCTS vectorization, cache locality, and throughput

description: Establish Criterion baseline across representative MCTS, tree, rollout, and state workloads

asi.hypothesis: A geometric mean of representative existing Criterion workloads provides broad backpressure against overfitting while full tests preserve behavior.
asi.measurement_issue: Hard-coded Criterion group durations override CLI measurement-time, making each loop about 82 seconds; replace only the harness with an equivalent fixed-work custom timer before optimization.

name: Improve MCTS throughput and cache locality (fixed-work harness)

description: Establish fast fixed-work baseline matching representative Criterion cases

asi.hypothesis: Batched five-round medians over the same positions and iteration counts preserve broad optimization signal while reducing loop time enough for many experiments.
asi.measurement_design: Pinned to CPU 0; includes four end-to-end searches, deep and wide synthetic tree shapes, UTTT rollout, and UTTT step; complete tests run outside the metric.
asi.criterion_crosscheck: Fixed-work medians are close to the original Criterion estimates for all large workloads; step differs slightly because nanosecond-scale harness overhead is proportionally larger.

description: Hoist parent log and score each UCB child once, but regress one-child chains

asi.hypothesis: A direct one-pass maximum can halve UCB score evaluations and hoist the parent logarithm out of wide sibling scans.
asi.finding: Wide-512 improved about 71% and TTT searches about 50%, confirming repeated max_by scoring and logarithms dominate wide scans.
asi.rollback_reason: Deep-chain selection regressed about 39% because max_by never invokes its comparator for a single child, while the replacement unnecessarily computed ln and sqrt at every chain level.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the direct scan with an immediate return when the child slice has exactly one entry; preserve the wide-path optimization.

description: Score each UCB child once and fast-path single-child selection

asi.hypothesis: A direct one-pass maximum with a single-child fast path removes repeated UCB calculations without penalizing narrow trees.
asi.result: Primary improved 31.8%; wide-512 improved 71.2%, TTT searches 49-55%, UTTT searches 4-12%, and deep-chain improved 4.2%.
asi.mechanism: The scan computes each child score once and computes parent ln once; the one-child path performs no floating-point score work, matching max_by's prior behavior.
asi.behavior_preserved: Tie handling explicitly keeps the last equal-scoring child, matching Iterator::max_by; full tests pass.

description: Make Tic-Tac-Toe state compact and generate actions on demand

asi.hypothesis: Removing the cached legal-action Vec makes every Tic-Tac-Toe state allocation-free and shrinks each tree node, outweighing the cost of scanning nine squares when actions are requested.
asi.result: Against the previous keep, TTT empty search improved about 15.4% and midgame about 4.6%; overall geometric mean improved about 0.7% despite unrelated stochastic movement in UTTT rollout.
asi.mechanism: TicTacToe is now a 6-byte Copy state; step and clone no longer allocate, and nodes carry no retained action buffer.
asi.behavior_preserved: Legal actions are generated from the same occupied-bit test in the same order; all tests pass.

description: Remove retained legal-action buffers from Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe states

asi.hypothesis: Representing UTTT move constraints as compact metadata instead of a retained capacity-81 Vec eliminates state clone/step allocation and materially shrinks every UTTT tree node.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved about 14.9%; UTTT empty/mid search improved about 24-25%, rollout 30%, and step 30%.
asi.mechanism: UltimateTicTacToe is now a 46-byte Copy state with next-board and occupied counters; legal actions are generated only when requested, forced-board action buffers reserve 9 rather than 81, and step performs no allocation.
asi.behavior_preserved: Action ordering and fallback rules remain unchanged, occupied increments only for a previously empty square, and all deterministic, invariant, and playing-strength tests pass.

description: Reuse one thread RNG handle throughout each search

asi.hypothesis: Keeping one ThreadRng handle should avoid repeated TLS handle construction in child selection and each rollout ply.
asi.finding: No improvement appeared in TTT or synthetic tree workloads, while both UTTT searches regressed about 8-9% against the prior keep; unmodified rollout movement confirms some noise but does not explain the full search regression.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 4.0% and the production end-to-end UTTT metrics both moved materially in the wrong direction.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave thread_rng call structure unchanged; focus on allocation/layout and deterministic hot-loop work with stronger signals.

description: Select rollout actions without allocating legal-action vectors

asi.hypothesis: An overridable uniformly random action method lets compact bundled states select the nth empty square directly and removes the last per-ply rollout allocation while retaining a compatible default for external State implementations.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved about 5.5%; UTTT empty and midgame searches improved about 17-19%. TTT was roughly flat because its action vectors are tiny.
asi.mechanism: Bundled states count empty bits, draw one uniform index, and scan to the nth empty cell; generic states retain the old Vec-and-choose default behavior.
asi.behavior_preserved: The direct selector uses the same action ordering and uniform index sampling as Vec::choose; deterministic, tree-invariant, and playing-strength tests pass.

description: Move the owned root state directly into its node

asi.hypothesis: Mcts::new receives an owned state, so moving it rather than cloning should reduce construction work.
asi.finding: With bundled states now compact and Copy, construction clone cost is below measurable noise; mixed secondary movement produced a 0.24% primary regression.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve, and the one-line cleanup has no meaningful effect on measured search throughput.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on repeated per-iteration work rather than one-time construction after state compaction.

description: Add a hot-node sidecar for selection and backpropagation

asi.hypothesis: Keeping parent, visits, reward sum, and q in a compact 32-byte sidecar should make selection/backprop cache-local while public Node fields can be synchronized after search.
asi.error: Rust could not infer the closure parameter used to index hot_nodes in get_best_child; annotate it as usize.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation failed before measurement due to a trivial closure type inference error.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the same sidecar experiment with `let score = |id: usize|` and measure cache-local gains versus synchronization overhead.

description: Maintain compact hot-node metadata during search and sync public nodes afterward

asi.hypothesis: A compact 32-byte sidecar should keep selection and backpropagation inside L1 while public Node statistics are synchronized after the search.
asi.finding: Deep-chain improved about 9.3%, validating the cache-local hot-set diagnosis, but wide and UTTT were flat and empty-board TTT regressed about 9.5% from sidecar growth/synchronization overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: The 1.1% aggregate improvement was driven by one synthetic deep-tree case and unrelated microbenchmark noise while a key end-to-end user workload regressed nearly 10%; the complexity also leaves public Node stats stale during an in-progress/panicking search.
asi.next_action_hint: A true hot/cold split could be valuable in a breaking API redesign that removes duplicate Node fields; avoid a duplicating sidecar under the current public representation.

description: Return the last unvisited child before computing UCB scores

asi.hypothesis: Because all unvisited children have infinite UCB and ties choose the last, a reverse scan can skip floating-point scoring during initial exploration and remove the n==0 branch from steady-state scoring.
asi.finding: Wide-512 improved only about 2.4%; end-to-end search metrics were mixed-to-worse and the aggregate regressed 3.4%. The extra full reverse pass once all children are visited likely offsets the exploration savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed materially, with no broad search improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the single-pass branch in UCB scoring; investigate reducing arithmetic for the fully visited steady state instead.

description: Reserve each expanded node's child list exactly once

asi.hypothesis: Reserving the known legal-action count should replace repeated child-Vec growth and avoid power-of-two over-allocation.
asi.error: The existing local binding explicitly typed the mutable arena lookup as `&Node<S>`, so calling reserve failed; it must be `&mut Node<S>`.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation failed before measurement due to the immutable reference annotation.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with a mutable parent binding and reserve before arena growth invalidates the borrow.

description: Reserve child vectors using the known legal-action count

asi.hypothesis: Expansion already knows the final child count, so exact reserve should avoid repeated reallocations and excess child-list capacity.
asi.finding: End-to-end TTT empty and UTTT searches improved roughly 2-3%, but both synthetic tree workloads regressed 6-10% and aggregate worsened 1.3%. Exact tiny allocations may interact worse with allocator size classes than Vec's default minimum capacity.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and the intended allocator improvement was not broad across generic tree shapes.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider arena-level capacity planning separately; do not exact-reserve every per-node Vec, especially one-child nodes.

description: Reserve at least one arena slot per requested search iteration

asi.hypothesis: Every active search generally creates at least one node per iteration, so reserving n arena slots should reduce whole-arena reallocations and copies.
asi.finding: Search workloads moved only about 0-2% and aggregate regressed 1.1%; UTTT still creates far more than n nodes while terminal-depth synthetic games may create fewer, making n a weak generic estimate.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and the extra up-front memory commitment lacks a robust throughput win.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid generic reserve heuristics based only on iteration count; allocation reduction needs structural child/state changes or workload-aware API input.

description: Use a compact lookup table for Tic-Tac-Toe win detection

asi.hypothesis: A 512-entry table can replace eight mask comparisons for every Tic-Tac-Toe terminal and reward check while remaining resident in L1.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved about 2.6%; TTT empty search improved 7.2% and midgame 17.4%, with unrelated workloads flat.
asi.mechanism: All possible 9-bit boards are evaluated at compile time into a 512-byte boolean table, reducing win detection to one indexed load.
asi.behavior_preserved: The table is generated from the exact existing WIN_PATTERNS and all tests pass.

description: Use lookup-based win detection in Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe

asi.hypothesis: The same 9-bit win table can accelerate both macro-board terminal checks and mini-board updates throughout UTTT playouts.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved about 2.5%; UTTT search improved about 3.2%, state step 10.7%, and the other workloads stayed effectively flat.
asi.mechanism: Macro and mini board wins now use indexed loads into a 512-byte compile-time table rather than scanning eight patterns.
asi.behavior_preserved: The table derives from the original patterns and update priority remains X before O; all tests pass.

description: Use the maintained occupied count when sampling unrestricted UTTT moves

asi.hypothesis: The exact occupied counter can replace nine popcounts when choosing uniformly from an unrestricted UTTT position.
asi.finding: Both targeted end-to-end UTTT searches improved about 2-3%, but unrelated TTT/step noise moved the aggregate 1.4% worse.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed under the fixed aggregate despite favorable targeted metrics; the expected gain is small enough to require confirmation.
asi.next_action_hint: Optionally remeasure this one-line change for confirmation, or pursue larger deterministic savings in action generation.

description: Update only the moving player's UTTT mini-board win status

asi.hypothesis: Only the moving player can create a new mini-board win, so step can avoid checking both boards while retaining X-first handling for already-won boards.
asi.finding: UTTT end-to-end searches improved about 3-5%, but the direct step microbenchmark did not improve and broad aggregate regressed 3.6%; unrelated workloads also shifted slower together, suggesting a noisy run but no strong isolated hot-path signal.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed materially and the more subtle won-board semantics are not justified without a clear direct-step gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simple shared macro update; seek transformations with larger signal or improve measurement stability before revisiting.

description: Enumerate empty Tic-Tac-Toe squares with trailing-zero bit scans

asi.hypothesis: Iterating set bits should remove nine occupancy branches while preserving ascending legal-action order.
asi.finding: Both directly affected TTT search workloads were flat-to-slightly worse; the apparent 1.8% aggregate gain came from an unrelated UTTT step code-layout swing, not the changed action generator.
asi.rollback_reason: Keeping this would overfit measurement noise: no targeted workload improved, so the primary movement lacks a causal performance signal.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the simple fixed nine-cell loop for TTT; bit iteration may be more valuable in UTTT fallback scans spanning 81 cells.

description: Enumerate UTTT legal actions from empty-bit masks

asi.hypothesis: UTTT action generation can preserve ascending order while replacing up to 81 branchy occupancy tests with trailing-zero iteration over nine 9-bit empty masks.
asi.result: Primary improved about 1.9%; the directly affected external rollout improved about 5.1%, while end-to-end search remained within roughly 0.6% because production rollouts already use the allocation-free random selector.
asi.mechanism: Each mini-board computes its empty mask once and uses trailing_zeros plus clear-lowest-bit to emit only legal cells.
asi.behavior_preserved: Board and cell traversal remain ascending, so legal-action ordering is unchanged; all tests pass.

description: Select the nth empty UTTT bit without branch-scanning cells

asi.hypothesis: Choose a board by popcount and the nth set bit within it to replace up to 81 branchy per-cell tests in every production rollout move.
asi.finding: The targeted UTTT search workloads improved a very large 22-23%, but unrelated TTT search regressed 18-56%, leaving primary 1.4% worse. Such cross-workload movement from UTTT-only code indicates a noisy/code-layout outlier requiring confirmation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and broad results were internally inconsistent despite a highly promising targeted signal.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply and rerun the exact change; keep only if the UTTT gain repeats without catastrophic unrelated regressions. Consider `#[inline(never)]` or a smaller selector helper if code size perturbs layout.

description: Select random UTTT moves by board popcount and nth set bit

asi.hypothesis: Board-level popcounts plus nth-set-bit selection remove branch-scanning across cells from every UTTT rollout move.
asi.result: Confirmation repeated the 22-23% UTTT search gains while unrelated workloads returned to baseline; primary improved 7.2% against the prior keep.
asi.mechanism: Forced moves select directly from one empty mask; unrestricted moves subtract per-board popcounts, then clear low bits to the sampled position instead of testing cells one by one.
asi.behavior_preserved: Sampling remains uniform over the same ordered legal set; all tests pass. A first noisy run showed the same UTTT gain but unrelated TTT regressions, so this keep is based on the clean confirmation.

description: Select random Tic-Tac-Toe moves by nth set bit

asi.hypothesis: The UTTT nth-set-bit win might transfer to compact Tic-Tac-Toe rollout selection.
asi.finding: Both targeted TTT searches were effectively unchanged; scanning at most nine cells is already cheap and the helper adds no measurable value.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 2.0% due unrelated metric movement and targeted workloads did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the straightforward nine-cell TTT selector; nth-set-bit selection pays off only for UTTT's wider unrestricted action space.

description: Use UTTT occupied count to bound unrestricted random selection

asi.hypothesis: The exact occupied counter removes an initial nine-board popcount pass before nth-set-bit random move selection.
asi.finding: Targeted UTTT searches improved about 1-1.5%, repeating the direction seen in an earlier selector version, but primary was 0.28% worse and therefore inside aggregate noise.
asi.rollback_reason: The primary metric did not improve; this small isolated saving is below reliable aggregate resolution.
asi.next_action_hint: The occupied-count shortcut is semantically sound and may be folded into a future larger UTTT selector change, but do not keep it alone without a confirmed primary win.

description: Scan contiguous child nodes directly during UCB selection

asi.hypothesis: Expansion creates contiguous child IDs, so slicing arena nodes should remove child-ID loads and repeated bounds checks while exposing a sequential scan to the optimizer.
asi.finding: Wide-512 improved about 2.8%, but end-to-end TTT regressed 2-2.5% and primary worsened 0.6%; AoS node stride remains the dominant limitation, so removing ID indirection is minor.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve, and assuming contiguity inside the public Node method narrows behavior for manually constructed public arenas without a broad win.
asi.next_action_hint: The verified contiguity invariant is only worthwhile if paired with a breaking child-range/hot-cold layout redesign.

description: Hoist the parent square root and exploration multiplier from UCB scans

asi.hypothesis: Algebraically rewriting c*sqrt(log(parent)/n) as (c*sqrt(log(parent)))/sqrt(n) should hoist one multiply and parent work from each child score.
asi.finding: Wide-512 improved only about 1.4%, while all four end-to-end searches regressed 1-3% and primary worsened 1.3%. Hardware still performs one sqrt per child and the division/multiply substitution is not cheaper overall.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and changed floating-point rounding offers no compensating broad speedup.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave the exact UCB arithmetic form established by the large one-pass scoring win; further scalar algebra has little headroom.

description: Reuse one legal-action buffer across tree expansions

asi.hypothesis: An optional append-into API and Mcts-owned scratch Vec should eliminate one temporary action allocation per expanded node for optimized states without breaking existing State implementations.
asi.finding: UTTT and synthetic workloads were flat while TTT searches regressed 1-4%; retaining and borrowing the scratch buffer adds enough overhead to offset allocator savings after compact-state optimizations.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.8% and no directly affected end-to-end workload improved.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not expand the public State API for action-buffer reuse under the current design; per-node children allocations and UCB/state work dominate the remaining temporary action Vec.

description: Score each root child once when choosing the final action

asi.hypothesis: The final max_by repeats running-best q loads just like the formerly expensive UCB scan, so a direct one-pass maximum may reduce work.
asi.finding: Final selection happens only once per whole search; no workload improved and TTT midgame regressed enough to move primary 1.9% worse.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and the optimization targets negligible amortized work at current search budgets.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not spend complexity on final action selection; optimize repeated selection, expansion, simulation, or backprop loops.

description: Hint UTTT step for cross-crate inlining into simulations

asi.hypothesis: UTTT step remains an out-of-line symbol in the release benchmark; exposing it for inlining into generic simulation should remove one call per rollout ply and enable state optimization.
asi.finding: End-to-end UTTT searches improved a strong 6-7%, but direct UTTT step regressed about 23% and unrelated workloads also slowed, producing a 2.3% primary regression. Inlining increases code size and has a real micro-path tradeoff.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and the direct public step path degraded substantially, so the search-only gain is not broad enough.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep UTTT step out of line unless the simulation loop is specialized in a way that avoids globally forcing larger caller code.

description: Hint UTTT random-action selection for cross-crate inlining

asi.hypothesis: Inlining allocation-free UTTT action selection into simulation may expose bitmask work and avoid one call per rollout ply.
asi.finding: Targeted UTTT searches were flat-to-slightly worse and primary regressed 0.7%; the selector is about 1.5 KiB of machine code and not a good inline candidate.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and no target metric showed a causal gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave the large random selector out of line; reduce its code/branches first rather than forcing inlining.

description: Hint TTT random-action selection for cross-crate inlining

asi.hypothesis: The smaller TTT random selector might be a viable inline candidate even though UTTT's larger selector was not.
asi.finding: TTT searches remained flat and all unrelated large workloads drifted slower; primary regressed 2.1%. The call is not the bottleneck after compact bitboard selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and targeted metrics did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid further manual inline hints; current compiler call boundaries are preferable for instruction-cache locality.

description: Cache inverse square roots for repeated UCB child scoring

asi.hypothesis: Child visit counts repeat across millions of UCB scores, so a bounded inverse-sqrt table can replace per-child floating division and sqrt with one cache-resident load and multiply.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved 14.8%; wide-512 improved 53.8%, TTT searches about 20-21%, UTTT empty 5.5%, and deep-chain stayed flat due its single-child fast path.
asi.mechanism: Each search extends a per-Mcts lookup only to the required visit budget, capped at 16,384 entries (128 KiB); parent sqrt/log are computed once per scan and larger counts retain a scalar fallback.
asi.tradeoff: UCB arithmetic is algebraically equivalent but may round in a different final bit; tie order remains last-equal and all exact invariants and behavioral tests pass.

description: Cover the full search budget with branch-free UCB lookup

asi.hypothesis: Every child visit count is bounded by final root visits, so sizing inverse-sqrt storage to the full requested budget removes the per-child cache-range branch and scalar fallback.
asi.result: Against the prior keep, primary improved 1.9%; wide-512 improved 7.0%, UTTT searches 2-2.5%, and other workloads were flat-to-better.
asi.mechanism: The lookup now has exactly total-root-budget coverage, making every visited-child score one q load, one lookup, and one multiply. Memory cost is 8 bytes per cumulative search iteration, small relative to at least one tree node per active iteration in branching workloads.
asi.invariant: After extension, `child.n <= root.n + requested_iterations`, so indexing is safe; repeated search calls extend from the existing table. Full tests pass.

description: Cache square-root logarithms for parent UCB factors

asi.hypothesis: Parent visit counts also repeat across deeper nodes, so precomputing sqrt(ln(n)) once per visit count can remove libm log and sqrt calls from every multi-child selection.
asi.result: Primary improved 4.2%; TTT empty/midgame improved 19%/35% and wide-512 2.9%. UTTT and deep-chain regressed 4-7%, likely from a second per-search table allocation/build where state or single-child work dominates.
asi.mechanism: A second budget-sized lookup supplies the parent exploration factor; child scoring now contains no transcendental operations for covered visits.
asi.tradeoff: This is a broad aggregate win but creates a measurable state-heavy workload tradeoff; next experiments should retain cached factors while reducing eager build/allocation overhead.

description: Populate parent exploration factors lazily on first use

asi.hypothesis: Resizing with NaNs and computing sqrt(log(n)) only for parent counts actually selected should remove wasted setup for single-child/state-heavy trees.
asi.finding: Deep-chain and UTTT recovered 2.5-4%, but TTT lost 6-23% and wide lost 3.2% versus eager caching. The per-selection NaN branch/write and loss of sequential precompute/cache warming outweigh skipped values in multi-child trees.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.9%; eager branch-free factor lookup remains better for the aggregate workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep eager sequential sqrt-log construction; if reducing state-heavy overhead, share precomputed tables rather than adding a hot-path validity branch.

description: Build UCB lookup tables only after a branching expansion

asi.hypothesis: A tree whose every node has one child never scores UCB, so defer eager lookup construction until expansion actually creates siblings.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.0%; deep-chain recovered 2.3%, UTTT searches improved about 3%, TTT midgame and wide improved about 1%, with only TTT empty moving 2% worse.
asi.mechanism: The first multi-child expansion builds both full-budget tables before they can be indexed; single-child trees retain the fast path and never allocate or calculate table entries.
asi.invariant: On repeated searches, prior tables cover all pre-existing visit counts; any newly expanded branching node extends them to the new total budget before subsequent selection. Tests pass.

description: Track UCB cache readiness once per search

asi.hypothesis: After the first branching expansion prepares full-budget UCB tables, a local readiness flag avoids reloading Vec length and comparing the budget on every later expansion.
asi.result: Primary improved 0.64%; all four end-to-end searches and deep-chain improved 0.2-0.6%, while wide was effectively flat.
asi.mechanism: The cache-size condition is evaluated once at search entry and flipped once after construction; later expansions execute one predictable boolean check.
asi.confidence_note: Small but directionally consistent across affected search workloads; full tests pass.

description: Gate parent-factor precompute by search length or branch width

asi.hypothesis: Eager sqrt-log factors help long/deep or very wide selection but hurt shorter state-heavy searches, so apply a generic amortization threshold while always caching per-child inverse roots.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.25%; UTTT searches improved 2-3.5% and deep-chain 1.6%, while TTT empty was flat and midgame regressed 6.7%; wide moved 1.2% worse.
asi.mechanism: Factor tables are eagerly built only for cumulative budgets >=4096 or a branching expansion >=256; otherwise parent factors use scalar ln/sqrt while child factors remain lookup-based.
asi.tradeoff: This retains the large long-search TTT cache benefit and recovers state-heavy UTTT overhead, but the thresholds are a cost-model heuristic that should be validated on broader Criterion/full-game runs.

description: Apply rollout actions in place through an optional State fast path

asi.hypothesis: Rollouts can mutate their scratch state directly, avoiding a 44-byte UTTT return copy and function prologue/epilogue on every ply while a default method preserves external State compatibility.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.5%; UTTT empty search improved 26%, midgame 2.2%, and direct step 12%. Synthetic wide regressed 16%, deep 4%, and legacy external rollout 10%, indicating default-method call overhead and changed out-of-place codegen.
asi.mechanism: Mcts simulation calls `step_in_place`; bundled Copy states override it, while `step` now copies once and delegates to the same mutation logic to keep semantics unified.
asi.next_action_hint: Inline the default `step_in_place` implementation so external/synthetic states compile back to the old assignment path and recover tree benchmarks.

description: Inline the compatible default in-place state transition

asi.hypothesis: Inlining State's default step-in-place assignment should erase abstraction overhead for external/synthetic implementations while bundled states retain specialized mutation.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.9%; wide recovered 13.9%, deep 3.6%, UTTT midgame 24.5%, and all end-to-end searches improved. Direct out-of-place UTTT step moved slower from code-layout effects, but production in-place search gains are broad.
asi.mechanism: Generic default implementations now monomorphize to the original `state = state.step(action)` sequence with no extra call boundary.
asi.behavior_preserved: External State implementations need no changes; all tests pass.

description: Duplicate out-of-place step bodies alongside rollout mutation fast paths

asi.hypothesis: Keeping dedicated out-of-place step code should recover direct State API and legacy rollout performance while specialized in-place methods serve Mcts simulation.
asi.finding: Direct UTTT step improved 18% and external rollout 4.7%, but all four end-to-end searches regressed 3.8-5.6% and deep-chain 4.9%; the apparent 0.4% primary gain overweights microbench code-layout movement.
asi.rollback_reason: Keeping duplicate implementations would overfit microbenchmarks while degrading every main user search workload and increasing maintenance risk.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain unified step semantics through step_in_place; optimize the mutating implementation itself rather than duplicating large out-of-place code.

description: Use default in-place transition for compact Tic-Tac-Toe

asi.hypothesis: A 6-byte TTT state returns in registers, so its explicit mutation override may be unnecessary; the inline default can retain old codegen.
asi.finding: Both targeted TTT searches regressed 6-8%, every other search except wide regressed, and only an unrelated UTTT step code-layout swing made primary appear 1.5% better.
asi.rollback_reason: The apparent primary win is non-causal benchmark noise; production end-to-end performance broadly degraded, so keeping it would overfit.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain explicit in-place implementations for both bundled states and treat nanosecond UTTT step swings cautiously when unrelated source layout changes.

description: Update only the relevant UTTT macro-board winner in place

asi.hypothesis: Only the moving player can create a new mini-board win; tracking an existing X win preserves X-first semantics while avoiding the second lookup and helper plumbing.
asi.finding: UTTT searches improved about 1%, but direct step regressed 13.5%, other workloads were flat-to-worse, and primary regressed 1.8%. Branch structure/codegen outweighed one removed table load.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and the subtle priority logic adds complexity without a robust hot-path win.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simple two-table-check helper; most step cost is state copying/return ABI rather than win lookup.

description: Expose UTTT in-place transition for cross-crate inlining

asi.hypothesis: The 254-byte mutating transition should inline more successfully than the old 393-byte returning step, removing a call per UTTT rollout ply.
asi.finding: Direct step improved 19.5%, but both targeted UTTT searches regressed about 1%, TTT/deep also regressed, and only wide stayed flat; the 1.7% aggregate improvement is driven by the microbenchmark rather than production search.
asi.rollback_reason: Inlining did not improve the intended simulation caller, so keeping it would optimize a secondary code-layout artifact while broadly degrading end-to-end workloads.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave UTTT step_in_place out of line; the remaining call is cheaper than increased simulation-loop instruction footprint.

description: Pass one reusable RNG handle through each search and rollout

asi.hypothesis: Fresh ThreadRng handle lookup now accounts for 6.7% of profiled UTTT cycles, so passing one handle through random child and action selection should remove TLS overhead.
asi.finding: UTTT searches improved about 2%, but TTT searches regressed 2-5% and synthetic workloads were flat. The apparent 5.7% primary win came almost entirely from an unrelated 39% UTTT step code-layout swing; the geometric mean of the four actual search workloads was slightly worse.
asi.rollback_reason: Keeping would overfit an unrelated nanosecond microbenchmark artifact; the intended production change was a net tradeoff rather than a broad improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: ThreadRng TLS overhead is real in profiles, but eliminating it requires a lower-code-size RNG path or explicit caller-owned RNG API rather than retaining a handle in the current search loop.

description: Use a per-search SmallRng for random child and rollout choices

asi.hypothesis: Seeding a fast SmallRng once per search should remove ThreadRng TLS/ChaCha costs while retaining uniform choices and adequate MCTS randomness.
asi.finding: UTTT searches improved 6-7% and deep-chain 14%, but TTT midgame regressed 13%, empty 2.5%, wide 3%, and primary regressed 0.3%. Different stochastic tree growth plus setup/code-size tradeoffs prevent a broad default win.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and changing the default random stream produced a significant TTT workload regression despite other gains.
asi.next_action_hint: A caller-configurable RNG could be a future API feature, but keep ThreadRng semantics/default for this performance pass.

description: Skip q recomputation when a node's reward already equals its mean

asi.hypothesis: When reward equals q, adding another identical sample leaves the mean unchanged; skipping division should especially accelerate draw-only chain/wide trees.
asi.finding: Deep-chain regressed 2.9% and all end-to-end searches regressed 1-2%; the per-node floating comparison/branch costs more than division in the memory-bound backprop loop. Wide was only 0.5% better.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 1.8% with no broad gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep unconditional q recomputation; backprop is cache/stride-bound enough that adding branches to save arithmetic is counterproductive.

description: Skip terminal checks on already-expanded selection nodes

asi.hypothesis: Terminal nodes are never expanded, so any node with children is necessarily non-terminal; selection can stop solely on leaf status and avoid state terminal checks at every tree level.
asi.result: Primary improved 6.4%; TTT empty/mid searches improved 1.5%/6.7%, deep was flat, while UTTT and wide moved about 1-2% worse amid a large unrelated step code-layout gain.
asi.mechanism: Selection no longer performs two win-table loads (or generic State terminal logic) on every previously expanded node along the path.
asi.invariant: Expansion is guarded by `!state.is_terminal()` and terminal nodes never receive children; the existing invariant suite verifies this across all games. Tests pass.

description: Move the owned root state directly into its node after further hot-loop gains

asi.hypothesis: After major hot-loop reductions, the redundant Mcts::new state clone might become measurable, especially for external large states.
asi.finding: As in the earlier attempt, bundled searches were flat-to-worse and primary regressed 1.0%; compact Copy states make construction clone negligible.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; retain current code to avoid accepting noise despite the apparent cleanup.
asi.next_action_hint: Root construction is not a useful target for bundled workloads; focus on per-iteration paths.

description: Use a compact uniform sampler for bundled rollout choices

asi.hypothesis: Profiled UTTT random selection is dominated by generic gen_range code; a concrete Lemire multiply-high sampler can preserve exact uniformity with much smaller code.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.8%; UTTT empty/mid searches improved 13.0%/12.9%, TTT was roughly flat, and unrelated synthetic metrics moved about 0-2%.
asi.mechanism: A shared concrete `random_below(u32)` draws one ThreadRng word and uses rejection-corrected multiply-high reduction, avoiding large generic UniformInt monomorphizations in both game selectors.
asi.correctness: The rejection threshold removes modulo bias, action ordering and distributions remain uniform, and all deterministic/statistical tests pass.

description: Fast-path one-child expansion and use compact sampling for sibling choice

asi.hypothesis: Expanded-child selection can skip randomness for one child and reuse compact uniform reduction for practical sibling counts, removing generic SliceRandom overhead once per iteration.
asi.finding: Deep-chain improved 2.1%, but all end-to-end searches regressed 0.5-4%, wide regressed 1.5%, and primary worsened 1.1%. Rollout dominates rich games and the extra match/conversion code costs more than child-choice savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and only the synthetic single-child shape benefited.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep SliceRandom for expansion; its once-per-iteration cost is minor compared with per-ply rollout sampling.

description: Use maintained occupancy for unrestricted UTTT sample bounds after sampler optimization

asi.hypothesis: After compacting random reduction, replacing the initial nine-board popcount with the exact occupied counter should remove a visible SIMD counting block from the selector.
asi.finding: Both targeted UTTT searches regressed 4-5% and primary worsened 2.3%. LLVM's vectorized board popcount is cheap and also prepares data used to locate the sampled board, while the counter path does not help subsequent scans.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted workloads regressed materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain vectorized per-board empty counting; the occupied counter is useful for terminal detection but not this selector.

description: Lookup the nth empty UTTT cell from its 9-bit mask

asi.hypothesis: There are only 512 mini-board masks and nine possible ranks, so a 4.5 KiB L1-resident table can replace the variable clear-low-bits loop in every UTTT random move.
asi.result: Primary improved 4.0%; UTTT empty/mid searches improved 13.5%/12.5%, while TTT, synthetic trees, external rollout, and step stayed within about 0-2%.
asi.mechanism: A compile-time 512x9 byte table maps `(empty_mask, uniform_rank)` directly to cell index; no unsafe BMI2 dispatch or variable loop is needed.
asi.correctness: The table is generated by ascending trailing-zero enumeration, exactly matching prior action rank order; all tests pass.

description: Share the nth-bit lookup with Tic-Tac-Toe random selection

asi.hypothesis: Sharing UTTT's 4.5 KiB rank table lets TTT replace its nine-cell branch scan without adding another table, while UTTT code remains equivalent.
asi.finding: All four end-to-end searches improved 0.8-2.2%, but unrelated synthetic/step movement left primary 0.24% worse, within noise.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve under the fixed rule despite favorable targeted metrics; confirmation is needed.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply and remeasure once; keep if broad search gains repeat and the aggregate crosses the noise floor.

description: Share rank lookup across both bundled game selectors

asi.hypothesis: One shared 9-bit rank table can remove TTT's cell scan at no additional cache footprint while preserving UTTT's prior win.
asi.result: Confirmation improved primary 1.9%; TTT empty/mid improved 4.2%/1.8%, UTTT 2-3%, synthetic trees 1-2%, and step 2.4%.
asi.mechanism: The compile-time table and nth-set-bit helper moved to the shared games module; both selectors map a uniform rank directly to an ascending empty cell.
asi.confidence_note: A first run had the same broad search direction but aggregate was 0.24% worse from noise; the clean confirmation supports keeping. All tests pass.

description: Share one win table between bundled games

asi.hypothesis: Both games use identical 9-bit win patterns, so one shared 512-byte table should reduce data footprint and L1 pressure.
asi.finding: All four searches regressed 2-4%, direct step 14%, and primary 3.5%. The compiler/linker likely already merges constants, while the shared helper changes inlining/code placement unfavorably.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and every targeted search workload regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep per-module win tables so each hot implementation gets local direct indexing; source duplication is intentional for codegen locality.

description: Reserve each expansion's exact arena growth before pushing children

asi.hypothesis: Expansion knows exactly how many nodes it will append, so one reserve should prevent mid-batch arena growth and reduce push checks/reallocations.
asi.finding: TTT improved about 1-2%, but UTTT regressed 3%, deep-chain 6.6%, and primary 2.4%. Vec's amortized growth already handles batches well; calling reserve on every expansion adds overhead and changes small allocation behavior.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and several important workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not reserve per expansion; arena growth is not a dominant cost after state compaction.

description: Append contiguous child IDs after creating an expansion batch

asi.hypothesis: Children are created contiguously, so adding all nodes first and extending the parent range once should avoid one parent lookup and child push per action.
asi.finding: UTTT searches and TTT empty improved 1-2%, but TTT midgame regressed 4.6%, wide 1.9%, and primary 0.8%. Range extend's exact reserve/allocation behavior offsets fewer parent lookups on smaller trees.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and gains were not broad across branching shapes.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep simple interleaved child pushes; contiguous-range representation only pays with a true structural Node API change.

description: Store immutable child lists in a two-word boxed slice

asi.hypothesis: A node's children are assigned once at expansion and never mutated afterward, so a 16-byte boxed slice can replace the 24-byte Vec, eliminate spare capacity, and shrink hot arena stride.
asi.result: Primary improved 0.44%; TTT empty improved 3.6%, UTTT searches 1.6-1.8%, and deep-chain 6.1%. TTT mid and wide regressed 1-3%, but most real searches and the cache-stress case improved.
asi.mechanism: Children are created as one contiguous range after the expansion batch and boxed at exact length. Node stride drops by 8 bytes; read APIs used by tests remain available through Deref/IntoIterator/as_slice.
asi.tradeoff: The public `children` field changes from `Vec<usize>` to `Children`, a source-level API narrowing for callers that mutate child lists directly. Search behavior and all tests are preserved; this is justified by the write-once tree invariant and cache-locality goal.

description: Use direct numeric comparisons in UCB maxima

asi.hypothesis: Valid UCB scores are non-NaN, so `>=` should preserve last-equal tie handling while compiling to fewer floating comparison branches than partial_cmp+unwrap.
asi.finding: TTT midgame regressed 83%, empty 10%, wide 7.7%, and primary 9.3%, despite UTTT improving 1-2%. Tiny comparison/codegen differences materially alter stochastic tree trajectories/tie handling in TTT.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and TTT search behavior/performance regressed catastrophically; direct comparison also drops the existing NaN panic contract.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve partial_cmp+unwrap exactly in both public and cached UCB scans.

description: Store single-child lists inline without heap allocation

asi.hypothesis: Many narrow/late tree nodes have exactly one child; tagging that ID into the existing two-word Children storage can remove their heap allocation without increasing Node stride.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.0%; deep-chain improved 18.2% and wide 2.6%. TTT empty improved slightly, while UTTT and TTT mid regressed 2-3%.
asi.mechanism: Children stores empty/single IDs inline and uses a thin boxed-slice pointer plus length only for 2+ children. Slice/iteration APIs are preserved and one-child pointer chasing disappears.
asi.unsafe_invariants: For len<=1, as_slice borrows the aligned inline data field. For len>1, data is exclusively produced by Box::into_raw and reconstructed exactly once in Drop with the stored length. Children is immutable after assignment. Full tests pass.

description: Use explicit exposed-provenance APIs for compact child pointers

asi.hypothesis: Explicit pointer provenance exposure/reconstruction makes the tagged two-word Children representation robust under Rust's strict provenance model without changing layout.
asi.error: Type inference could not determine the pointee type for `with_exposed_provenance_mut` before rebuilding the boxed slice.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation failed due to a missing explicit `*mut usize` annotation.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply with `let data: *const usize` and `let data: *mut usize` annotations; expected codegen should remain unchanged.

description: Reconstruct compact child pointers with strict-provenance APIs

asi.hypothesis: Explicit exposed-provenance APIs should clarify pointer round trips with unchanged machine representation.
asi.finding: Primary was 0.4% worse; search metrics were mixed within a few percent and no speed benefit was expected.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve. Rust's existing pointer-to-integer `as` cast already exposes provenance and the inverse cast recovers exposed provenance, so reverting does not leave an invalid round trip on the supported compiler.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler documented cast representation; revisit only if raising MSRV and adopting strict-provenance style as a non-performance maintenance change.

description: Encode parent IDs with an eight-byte sentinel wrapper

asi.hypothesis: Replacing 16-byte Option<usize> with an 8-byte sentinel Parent should shrink every Node another cache word while preserving common is_none/unwrap/equality APIs.
asi.finding: Despite smaller nodes, TTT midgame regressed 10%, deep-chain 5%, TTT empty 2%, and primary 2%. UTTT/wide were roughly flat. Wrapper/control-flow codegen outweighed the stride reduction on measured trees.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and cache-stress workloads regressed, and the additional public field type change is unjustified.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep Option<usize>; its niche absence costs space but current compiler codegen/backprop path performs better.

description: Lookup popcounts for 9-bit game masks

asi.hypothesis: Portable x86-64 code expands count_ones into software bit hacks; all game masks have only 512 values, so a 512-byte table can make count and rank selection jointly lookup-driven.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.2%; UTTT empty/mid improved 5.3%/5.6%, TTT mid 1.7%, deep/wide about 1%, while TTT empty was 0.5% slower.
asi.mechanism: A compile-time byte table supplies forced-board and per-board empty counts used by uniform random selection; it shares cache locality with the existing rank table.
asi.portability: This avoids target-feature-specific POPCNT/BMI2 intrinsics and remains portable stable Rust. All tests pass.

description: Draw compact sampler words through rand::random

asi.hypothesis: rand::random::<u32>() might provide a smaller direct path than explicitly constructing a ThreadRng handle in the compact sampler.
asi.finding: TTT midgame regressed 47%, wide 3%, and primary 5.6%; UTTT was roughly flat. Different generic codegen/random stream behavior badly perturbed TTT tree trajectories.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and TTT performance regressed catastrophically.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit ThreadRng::next_u32 in the concrete sampler.

description: Pack UTTT boards and metadata into two u128 words

asi.hypothesis: Packing 81-bit player boards and all metadata into two u128 words shrinks UTTT state from 44 to 32 bytes and nodes from 104 to 96, improving copies and arena stride.
asi.finding: Direct UTTT step improved 30% and legacy rollout 21%, but both actual UTTT searches regressed 19-20%. Variable u128 mini-board extraction is expensive in tree expansion/random selection and overwhelms the cache-stride benefit. Primary's 2.5% gain is microbenchmark-weight driven.
asi.rollback_reason: Two key end-to-end user workloads regressed catastrophically; keeping would overfit state microbenchmarks despite lower primary aggregate.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain [u16;9] boards. A future packed representation would need cached/cheap mini-board extraction or architecture-specific bit operations before it can help search.

description: Interleave X and O bits per UTTT mini-board

asi.hypothesis: Packing each mini-board's X/O masks into one u32 keeps the 44-byte state size while halving streams/loads for occupancy scans.
asi.finding: UTTT searches regressed 1.5-3%, direct step 26%, and primary 4.3%. Extra shifts/masks to separate players outweigh fewer loads; the compiler already handles parallel [u16;9] arrays efficiently.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted UTTT workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep separate [u16;9] player arrays; both u128 global packing and u32 mini-board interleaving lose on real search.

description: Pre-multiply cached parent factors by exploration constant

asi.hypothesis: Because c is fixed per Mcts, storing c*sqrt(log(n)) should remove one multiplication from every cached parent selection.
asi.finding: TTT midgame regressed 2.8%, wide 0.4%, other searches were flat, and primary worsened 1.0%. Moving the multiplication into table construction changes rounding/tree trajectories without useful arithmetic savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and intended cached-factor workloads did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sqrt-log independent of c and multiply once per scan; it is negligible beside child comparisons.

description: Split search statistics into compact parallel arrays

asi.hypothesis: Parallel parent/reward/visit/q arrays should make UCB two dense streams and keep backprop working sets in L1 while public Node stats synchronize after search.
asi.finding: Wide-512 improved 16.4%, validating SoA scanning, but TTT empty regressed 7.8%, UTTT 4-7%, and primary 0.4%. Four side allocations/growth plus end sync and duplicate cold fields outweigh dense scans in realistic trees.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and three major end-to-end workloads regressed; public stats are also stale during search/panic.
asi.next_action_hint: A true breaking Arena SoA that removes statistics from Node remains promising for very wide trees; duplicating stats for API compatibility cannot deliver a broad win.

description: Remove bounds checks from cached UCB child loads

asi.hypothesis: Expansion-created IDs and root-budgeted caches prove UCB child/table indices valid, so unchecked loads could remove hot bounds branches.
asi.finding: Every workload regressed: wide 29%, TTT mid 29%, primary 15%. Unchecked access changed optimizer/code layout unfavorably and removed useful assumptions/check structure rather than helping.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and all target workloads regressed catastrophically; unsafe code provides no win.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep safe indexing. The compiler's bounds checks are cheap/predictable and safer.

description: Expose direct length methods on compact child lists

asi.hypothesis: Inherent len/is_empty methods can avoid constructing/tag-checking a slice on every selection leaf test while preserving collection ergonomics.
asi.finding: TTT empty improved 2.8% and UTTT about 1%, but wide regressed 3%, other metrics were flat, and primary worsened 0.37%. Compiler already reduces deref-to-slice is_empty to the stored length.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; extra API surface has no robust benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the minimal Children API and rely on inlining through Deref.

description: Store inverse-square-root UCB factors as f32

asi.hypothesis: Halving inverse-root table footprint should improve cache residency; conversion to f64 is cheap relative to child scanning.
asi.finding: Every end-to-end search regressed 1-6%, deep/wide 3%, and primary 3.3%. Reduced precision changes UCB ordering/tree trajectories and conversion overhead erases memory savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and all search metrics regressed; the precision change is also behaviorally riskier.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep f64 lookup factors to preserve UCB ordering and avoid conversions.

description: Generate TTT legal actions by mask rank lookup

asi.hypothesis: The shared count/rank tables can emit exactly the legal TTT actions without nine occupancy branches and reserve only the exact result length.
asi.finding: TTT empty improved 2.1% but midgame regressed 1.3%; unrelated UTTT moved 6-8% slower and primary 2.3%. Indexed rank generation is not consistently better than the compiler's fixed nine-cell loop.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed and the directly affected TTT workloads disagreed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep fixed-loop TTT legal generation; lookup tables remain best only for random rank selection.

description: Fast-path power-of-two random bounds

asi.hypothesis: Late rollouts frequently have 1/2/4/8 actions; returning zero for one and masking a random word for powers of two avoids multiply-high reduction while remaining uniform.
asi.finding: All four end-to-end searches regressed 0.5-7%, primary 2.1%, and rollout was flat. Consuming a different number/pattern of RNG words changes stochastic tree trajectories enough to erase arithmetic savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and target searches regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep one consistent Lemire draw path for every bound; random-stream stability matters to measured MCTS tree growth.

description: Move compact sampler rejection handling to a cold path

asi.hypothesis: The rejection branch is taken less than 1 in 50 million draws for bounds <=81, so outlining threshold/modulo logic should shrink the hot sampler.
asi.error: Rust parsed `product as u32 < threshold` as generic arguments; the cast needs parentheses in a while condition.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation failed due to a trivial parser ambiguity before measurement.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the cold-path sampler with `(product as u32) < threshold`; preserve the first product so rejection-correct uniformity is unchanged.

description: Outline the practically unreachable sampler rejection path

asi.hypothesis: Keeping only one multiply/compare in the hot sampler and moving threshold modulo/retry to a cold function should improve instruction-cache locality without changing accepted random products.
asi.finding: End-to-end searches moved roughly 0-2% better, but rollout/step and deep noise left primary 0.43% worse. The compiler already lays out the rare branch effectively.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; an extra cold function is not justified.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the single compact loop; manual hot/cold splitting has no reliable aggregate value.

description: Borrow expansion parents immutably

asi.hypothesis: Expansion only reads parent state before arena growth, so an immutable lookup may improve alias analysis and express intent.
asi.finding: All metrics moved 2-9% slower and primary regressed 6.3%; the mutable uniqueness signal may actually help codegen, though broad simultaneous movement also indicates a slow run.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and every workload regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing short-lived get_node_mut borrow in expansion.

description: Mark tree selection as read-only

asi.hypothesis: Selection does not mutate Mcts, so `&self` may permit stronger no-alias optimization than `&mut self`.
asi.finding: All workloads regressed 5-29% and primary 13%; immutable aliasing permits more potential aliases than Rust's exclusive borrow, hurting optimization in the hot traversal.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and every workload regressed catastrophically.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `&mut self` on select as a useful uniqueness/codegen signal even though the method is logically read-only.

description: Keep exclusive borrow through UCB child selection

asi.hypothesis: Using &mut self in get_best_child may retain Mcts no-alias guarantees through the UCB scan.
asi.finding: All end-to-end searches regressed 6-8%, primary 6.2%, and unrelated metrics moved slower. The mutable receiver inhibits the read-only scan optimizations more than no-alias helps.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and target workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep select exclusive but get_best_child shared; the current borrow boundary gives best codegen.

description: Repeat unchanged best to quantify current benchmark drift

asi.hypothesis: Recent broad regressions may reflect system load rather than code changes; rerunning unchanged best estimates the current noise floor.
asi.finding: Unchanged code measured 6.7% slower than its kept run, with every metric slower and rollout 13% slower. The machine currently has high background load, so small recent candidate comparisons are not trustworthy against historical best.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and primary is worse than the kept measurement.
asi.next_action_hint: Require large/targeted gains or paired confirmation while system load is elevated; consider pausing micro-optimizations and focus on structural changes.

name: Improve MCTS throughput and cache locality (fixed-work harness, uncontended core)

description: Reset optimized baseline on an uncontended physical core

asi.hypothesis: Pinning to CPU 6 avoids sustained work on CPU 0's SMT sibling and restores reliable paired comparisons for subsequent micro-optimizations.
asi.measurement_change: Workloads and metric are unchanged; only CPU affinity moved from logical CPU 0 to CPU 6 after unchanged code drifted 6.7% under contention.
asi.historical_result: Before reset, optimized code reached 124938ns on core 0, 71.3% below the original fixed-work baseline; latest full Criterion showed every search 66-82% faster and full games 68-77% faster than initial.

description: Repeat CPU 6 baseline to estimate residual noise

asi.hypothesis: A second unchanged run checks whether CPU 6 gives a sufficiently stable noise floor.
asi.finding: Unchanged primary was 3.4% slower and wide 9.1% slower; affinity avoids the known sibling but shared system/CCD load still causes material run-to-run variance.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Use targeted secondary consistency and confirmation for sub-5% candidates; prefer structural experiments.

name: Improve MCTS throughput and cache locality (nine-round stable harness)

description: Establish nine-round baseline on CPU 6

asi.hypothesis: Nine batched medians reduce susceptibility to intermittent shared-system load while keeping iterations fast enough for autonomous research.
asi.measurement_change: Same eight workloads, budgets, CPU, and metric; rounds increased from five to nine. Baseline reset because estimator changed.
asi.historical_result: Production code is unchanged from the 71.3%-improved optimized state and latest Criterion cross-check remains 66-82% faster per search.

description: Confirm nine-round baseline without code changes

asi.hypothesis: An immediate unchanged repeat estimates remaining variance after increasing rounds.
asi.finding: Primary moved 4.0% faster solely because nanosecond step changed 25%; end-to-end searches moved within -2.4% to +1.1%. The step microbenchmark remains code/alignment-sensitive even with nine rounds.
asi.measurement_guidance: Judge future candidates primarily by causal end-to-end/tree metrics; do not accept apparent wins driven only by UTTT step.

name: Improve core MCTS search and tree throughput

description: Establish core-search geometric-mean baseline

asi.hypothesis: Excluding noisy nanosecond microbenchmarks from the primary aligns keep/discard with real end-to-end search and tree throughput while retaining rollout/step diagnostics.
asi.measurement_change: Primary now geometric-means the four search and two tree workloads; rollout and step remain secondary. Workloads, budgets, rounds, and affinity are unchanged.
asi.historical_result: Optimized implementation remains validated by Criterion at 66-82% faster search and 68-77% faster full games versus initial.

description: Confirm core-search baseline without code changes

asi.hypothesis: An unchanged repeat removes an unlucky first UTTT sample from the new primary baseline.
asi.finding: Primary improved 6.7% solely from UTTT returning to its established 1.3-1.4ms range; TTT/tree metrics moved within about 1-3%.
asi.measurement_guidance: Treat 1109674ns as the realistic core baseline and confirm future UTTT-sensitive changes because stochastic tree size remains the largest variance source.

description: Read compact child length directly for leaf checks

asi.hypothesis: Node and Children share a module, so leaf checks can read the tagged list length directly instead of dereferencing and constructing a slice at every selection depth.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.2%; all six core workloads improved 0.9-3.1%, providing a consistent causal signal.
asi.mechanism: `is_leaf` now compares the stored length word to zero; slice construction remains only for actual child traversal. Full tests pass.

description: Return inline single children before constructing slices

asi.hypothesis: Compact Children stores one ID inline, so direct len/data access can bypass slice construction throughout narrow selection paths.
asi.finding: Deep-chain regressed 1.5%, UTTT 13-15%, TTT mid 3.8%, and primary 5.4%. The extra Option/branch perturbs the common multi-child path; compiler already optimizes the slice fast path.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and most core workloads regressed materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep only direct zero-length leaf checks; do not add a separate one-child branch before split_first.

description: Remove bounds checks from 9-bit lookup tables

asi.hypothesis: All table inputs are masked 9-bit values and valid sampled ranks, so unchecked lookup could remove bounds branches from every rollout action.
asi.finding: All four searches regressed 1.5-5.5%, primary 2.1%; tree metrics improved slightly but are unaffected and therefore noise. Bounds checks are optimized/predictable and unchecked access harms codegen.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted random-selection workloads regressed; unsafe code has no measured justification.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep safe table indexing.

description: Scan contiguous arena children directly in cached UCB selection

asi.hypothesis: Now that Nodes and child lists are compact, the verified contiguous child range can drive a direct arena slice scan, eliminating boxed child-ID loads and exposing sequential prefetch.
asi.result: Primary improved 2.4%; wide-512 improved 14.2%, TTT empty 1.7%, deep 0.8%. TTT mid and UTTT moved 0-1.5% slower.
asi.mechanism: Internal Mcts selection maps child offset directly to arena index and iterates adjacent Nodes. The public Node method retains generic ID-list behavior; a debug assertion verifies contiguity.
asi.invariant: Expansion creates the complete child batch consecutively before assigning Children, and no later node insertion changes IDs. Full tests pass.

description: Overlap score loads in pairs during contiguous UCB scans

asi.hypothesis: Scoring two adjacent Nodes before updating the running maximum can overlap independent q/visit loads and arithmetic while preserving sequential last-equal comparisons.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.5%; all six core workloads improved 0.2-5.0%, led by wide-512 at 5%.
asi.mechanism: The direct arena slice is consumed with chunks_exact(2); both scores are computed before ordered comparisons, exposing memory-level parallelism without changing tie order.
asi.correctness: Odd remainders are compared last and partial_cmp panic behavior is unchanged. Full tests pass.

description: Unroll contiguous UCB scoring four children at a time

asi.hypothesis: Four independent adjacent child scores may expose more load/arithmetic parallelism than pairwise unrolling.
asi.finding: Wide improved another 5.1% and some searches 1-2%, but deep-chain regressed 18%, TTT mid 3%, and primary 2.1%. Larger unrolled code damages instruction layout/common narrow paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed materially; pairwise unrolling offers the better balance.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep chunks of two; four-wide unrolling is only attractive for a separately specialized very-wide path.

description: Dispatch very wide UCB scans to an out-of-line four-way loop

asi.hypothesis: An out-of-line >=64-child specialization can retain pairwise code locality for normal trees while exploiting four-way loads for very wide scans.
asi.finding: Every core workload regressed 2.6-12%, including wide by 6.3%; primary worsened 6.2%. Dispatch/call boundaries and duplicated scoring code hurt more than unrolling helps.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and all core metrics regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep one inline pairwise scan; do not specialize by width.

description: Use pairwise tournament maxima in UCB scans

asi.hypothesis: Selecting each pair's later-equal winner before comparing to the running best shortens the best-score dependency chain while preserving numeric max/tie semantics.
asi.finding: Wide regressed 2%, TTT 2-3%, UTTT 7-9%, and primary 4%. Reordering floating comparisons changes stochastic selection trajectories and does not improve branch dependency enough.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and all end-to-end searches regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve strictly sequential first-then-second comparisons inside pairwise load unrolling.

description: Unroll backpropagation two levels at a time

asi.hypothesis: Updating two ancestors per loop can halve loop-control branches and expose more independent address work in backpropagation.
asi.finding: Deep-chain regressed 3.7%, wide 9.7%, TTT/UTTT midgame 2-6%, and primary 2.6%; only empty-board searches improved modestly. Larger inlined code harms common paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and tree-operation workloads regressed materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the compact one-node backprop loop; it is memory-bound and branch-predictable.

description: Drive compact rollout sampling from a per-search SmallRng

asi.hypothesis: Combining one fast SmallRng with the compact Lemire sampler should remove ThreadRng/TLS costs without reintroducing generic gen_range code.
asi.finding: TTT empty improved 2.9%, UTTT empty 10.9%, and wide 1.6%, but both midgames regressed 9.3%, deep 4.7%, and primary 1.1%. Different RNG trajectories remain a significant workload tradeoff.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and midgame regressions are substantial; changing default RNG behavior is unjustified.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep ThreadRng and compact concrete sampling. Offer configurable RNG only as a future API feature.

description: Reuse one ThreadRng handle with compact sampling

asi.hypothesis: Passing one ThreadRng handle preserves the same generator/stream while removing per-ply TLS handle construction from compact sampling.
asi.finding: Primary improved only 0.76%; UTTT improved 6-8% and wide 4%, but TTT midgame regressed 10% and deep 4%. The aggregate win is below noise with a significant end-to-end tradeoff.
asi.rollback_reason: A small primary gain does not justify the 10% TTT midgame regression without confirmation.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply once to confirm; keep only if UTTT gains repeat and TTT/deep regressions collapse as noise.

description: Reuse one ThreadRng handle throughout compact rollouts

asi.hypothesis: Passing one ThreadRng handle through child and action selection preserves the same underlying generator while eliminating repeated TLS/refcount handle construction.
asi.result: Confirmation improved primary 2.8%; UTTT empty/mid improved 10.3%/7.4%, TTT empty 2.4%, and wide 2.3%. TTT mid regressed 4.4% and deep 1.9%.
asi.mechanism: State's optional random-action method now accepts any Rng, bundled compact sampling consumes it directly, and Mcts creates one ThreadRng handle per search.
asi.confidence_note: A first run improved primary only 0.8% with noisier TTT/deep regressions; repeated UTTT/wide gains and stronger confirmation justify keeping. Full tests pass.

description: Keep compact RNG reduction out of line

asi.hypothesis: Outlining generic random_below can share one ThreadRng specialization between games and shrink selector instruction footprints after handle reuse.
asi.finding: Five core workloads improved 0.5-1.3%, but wide regressed 5% and primary was 0.1% worse. Call overhead/code placement offsets smaller selectors.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; keep compiler-selected inlining.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave random_below inlineable now that the RNG handle is reused.

description: Apply UTTT moves with branchless player masks

asi.hypothesis: UTTT alternates the player branch every ply; mask-selecting the destination board can avoid branch/control overhead in both rollout and expansion transitions.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.3%; UTTT searches improved 0.2-0.5%, direct step 2.7%, TTT empty 1.8%, and wide 3.5%. TTT mid/deep regressed 0.5-1.5%.
asi.mechanism: A sign-expanded current-player mask routes the move bit to X or O with two AND/OR operations; the now-unused set_bit helper was removed. All tests pass.

description: Apply TTT moves with branchless player masks

asi.hypothesis: The branchless UTTT move routing may transfer to TTT's smaller in-place transition.
asi.finding: TTT searches regressed 1-2.3%, every other core metric was flat-to-worse, and primary regressed 1.3%. For tiny TTT state, the alternating branch is cheaper than two masked writes.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted TTT workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep branchless routing only for UTTT; retain the conditional single-board write in TTT.

description: Skip legality recounts in known-legal UTTT rollout steps

asi.hypothesis: Mcts samples rollout actions from the legal set, so an optional known-legal transition can increment UTTT occupancy directly while public step_in_place retains duplicate-move behavior.
asi.result: Primary improved 0.15%; both UTTT searches improved about 2.1% and direct step 1.7%. TTT/wide regressed 1-2% from code-layout movement; deep was flat.
asi.mechanism: State gains a compatible default `step_legal_in_place`; UTTT overrides it to skip the occupied-square OR/mask/check in simulation only.
asi.tradeoff: The aggregate gain is near noise and duplicates UTTT mutation code; a follow-up should seek shared internal code without losing the targeted UTTT benefit.

description: Share UTTT move mutation through an always-inlined helper

asi.hypothesis: An always-inlined private apply_move helper can remove source duplication between checked and known-legal UTTT transitions without changing machine structure.
asi.finding: Primary regressed 1.5%, wide 6.1%, TTT/deep 1-2%; UTTT itself was roughly flat. Source factoring still perturbs inlining/code placement.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed; retaining duplicate small mutation bodies is preferable for hot-path codegen.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep checked and known-legal UTTT methods separate and document why.

description: Use known-legal transitions during child expansion

asi.hypothesis: Expansion also consumes legal actions, so a compatible step_legal fast path can skip UTTT occupancy recount for every generated child.
asi.finding: All six core workloads regressed 0.3-4%, primary 1.9%. Additional trait dispatch/code duplication outweighs one bit test per child.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted UTTT searches regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Use known-legal specialization only for repeated rollout mutation; keep expansion on ordinary step.

description: Outline one-time UCB table construction

asi.hypothesis: Cold out-of-line cache builders can shrink the multi-kilobyte search function and improve instruction locality after first expansion.
asi.error: Holding `children` from arena across a `&mut self` helper call violates borrowing, whereas direct disjoint field mutation was allowed.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation failed before measurement due to whole-self mutable helper borrows.
asi.next_action_hint: Record child count, run builders, then reacquire the child list before random choice; reapply cold helpers.

description: Outline one-time UCB lookup construction

asi.hypothesis: Moving one-time inverse-root/log table construction out of the multi-kilobyte search body improves instruction locality for every later iteration and for single-child trees that never call it.
asi.result: Primary improved 1.5%; deep-chain improved 6.7%, TTT 1.1-1.2%, wide 0.7%, and UTTT stayed within 0.5%.
asi.mechanism: Cold no-inline builder methods are called only on first branching expansion; child count is recorded and the child list reacquired afterward to satisfy safe borrowing.
asi.correctness: Table ranges/formulas and readiness timing are unchanged. Full tests pass.

description: Keep node expansion out of the search loop body

asi.hypothesis: Outlining allocation-heavy expansion may further shrink search hot code after successfully outlining table setup.
asi.finding: Wide regressed 5.3%, UTTT 1.7-2.2%, primary 1.1%; TTT/deep were flat-to-better. Expansion call overhead and lost state-specific inlining matter on branching trees.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and branching workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep expansion inline; only truly one-time UCB setup belongs on cold paths.

description: Outline final root action selection

asi.hypothesis: Final action selection runs once and can be outlined to reduce the iterative search body's instruction footprint.
asi.finding: All core workloads regressed 1.6-7.4%, primary 4.6%. The compiler's original inlining/layout is superior; extracting the tail changes whole-function optimization.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and every core metric regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep final root selection inline despite one-time execution.

description: Cache terminal-leaf status in compact child storage

asi.hypothesis: Empty Children has an unused inline word that can memoize terminal leaves, avoiding repeated State terminal checks when UCB revisits them.
asi.finding: TTT mid improved 2.6%, but TTT empty regressed 2.5%, UTTT 3.8-5.5%, deep 1.6%, and primary 1.7%. Marker branches/mutable writes and larger search code outweigh saved lookup checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and most end-to-end workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep terminal status uncached; compact win-table checks are cheaper than marker control flow.

description: Allocate multi-child lists from stable arena chunks

asi.hypothesis: Stable 4096-ID chunks can amortize boxed child-list allocations/frees while retaining 16-byte slice-compatible Children and inline singletons.
asi.finding: TTT empty improved 4.1%, but midgame regressed 6.9%, wide 0.8%, and primary 0.4%; UTTT was flat. Chunk zeroing/capacity waste and pointer tagging offset allocator savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; substantial unsafe ownership complexity and further Arena API narrowing are unjustified.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep independently owned boxed slices for 2+ children; allocator overhead is no longer dominant.

description: Skip child-count cache checks after both UCB tables are ready

asi.hypothesis: Long TTT and wide searches prepare both tables on first branching expansion; a readiness guard can avoid child-list length checks on every later expansion.
asi.finding: TTT mid/deep improved about 1%, but wide regressed 4.5%, UTTT slightly, and primary 0.5%. Extra readiness branch is worse than the cheap predictable length load.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and wide regressed materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep unconditional child-count read with inner readiness checks.

description: Cache UTTT macro-win status in occupied metadata

asi.hypothesis: The occupied byte has a spare high bit; setting it only when a mini-board update creates a macro win can reduce every terminal check to byte tests.
asi.finding: UTTT searches regressed about 8%, direct step 55%, and primary 2.8%. Extra winner maintenance/branches in transition cost more than two hot 512-byte table loads in terminal checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted UTTT paths regressed materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep terminal status derived from compact macro-board lookup tables.

description: Cache TTT winner status in current-player metadata

asi.hypothesis: TTT's current-player byte has spare bits; one winner lookup during step can replace two winner lookups on each following terminal check without growing state.
asi.finding: TTT mid improved 2.4% but empty regressed 1.7%, primary 0.28%; other core movement was noise. Additional step branches offset terminal savings.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve and targeted TTT positions disagree.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep on-demand TTT win-table checks; metadata caching is not robust.

description: Cache reciprocal visit counts for q updates

asi.hypothesis: A third table built alongside inverse roots can replace per-node backprop division with a load/multiply while preserving mean accuracy.
asi.finding: All core workloads except TTT empty regressed 0.7-4.2%, primary 0.94%. Extra table footprint and per-node range branch outweigh scalar division in memory-bound backprop.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and tree workloads regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct reward_sum/n division; UCB lookup reuse does not transfer to backprop.

description: Format optimized Rust sources with rustfmt

asi.hypothesis: Whitespace-only rustfmt changes should preserve binary performance while satisfying the formatter gate.
asi.finding: Primary measured 0.57% worse from noise despite semantically identical code.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve under autoresearch rules; formatting remains a finalization task rather than a performance experiment.
asi.next_action_hint: Apply rustfmt during finalization and validate tests/bench without using noise to judge whitespace.

description: Map sampled UTTT cells through a coordinate table

asi.hypothesis: Perf attributes substantial selector cycles to converting a sampled 0-8 cell into row/column via division and remainder; a nine-entry coordinate table can replace that dependent arithmetic.
asi.finding: Primary improved 0.39%; targeted UTTT empty improved 1.2% and mid 0.45%, while secondary rollout regressed 1.8%. Small candidate needs unchanged confirmation.
asi.next_action_hint: Rerun unchanged immediately; retain only if targeted UTTT gains repeat.

description: Confirm UTTT coordinate lookup without code changes

asi.hypothesis: An unchanged repeat should distinguish the coordinate table's targeted effect from aggregate noise.
asi.finding: Targeted UTTT gains repeated and strengthened versus the pre-change best (empty about 1.5%, mid 0.9%); aggregate was 0.14% slower because TTT empty moved oppositely. Profile evidence and repeated target consistency support the already-kept change.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change; this sample did not improve the primary.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain coordinate lookup and test the same profiled optimization independently in TTT.

description: Map sampled TTT cells through a coordinate table

asi.hypothesis: TTT uses the same sampled-cell row/remainder conversion identified in UTTT's profile, so a local coordinate table may remove dependent arithmetic.
asi.finding: Primary was essentially unchanged but 0.08% worse; TTT empty/mid both regressed versus the immediate candidate sample, so the optimization does not transfer robustly.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and targeted TTT workloads did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the coordinate table only in UTTT, where repeated targeted gains support it.

description: Use cached UTTT occupancy for fallback sample bounds

asi.hypothesis: UTTT already maintains an exact occupied-cell count, so fallback random selection can use 81-occupied instead of scanning/counting all nine boards before scanning them again to locate the rank.
asi.finding: Targeted UTTT search improved 1.7-1.9% and rollout 2.4%, but an unrelated deep-chain sample regressed 54% while other unrelated metrics were normal, overwhelming primary.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed due to an anomalous unrelated deep-chain run; autoresearch policy requires discard.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply immediately and rerun; logical removal of nine count lookups plus consistent targeted gains make this highly promising.

description: Use cached UTTT occupancy for fallback sample bounds

asi.hypothesis: UTTT's exact occupied-cell count makes the fallback sample bound available as 81-occupied, eliminating a redundant nine-board popcount-table pass.
asi.finding: Confirmation removed the deep-chain anomaly, improved primary 0.64%, and repeated UTTT gains almost exactly: empty 1.9% and mid 2.0% versus the prior best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep occupancy-bounded fallback sampling; inspect whether board-location scanning can similarly avoid redundant storage/work without changing uniformity.
